title: Trump May Still Attack

source.title: Iranian leaders welcome US midterms, but Trump may still attack
source.note: published 11-04 15:13 UTC; the 11-04 sweep matched it on 'iran', 'tehran', 'midterm'. Read in full via the cloud fetch as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. Twenty-six paragraphs: the article (Motamedi, from Tehran), three Iranian officials (Ghalibaf, Mohseni-Ejei, a statement attributed to Khamenei — his first on the Press), three analysts (Vakil of Chatham House, Azizi of Crisis Group, Slavin of Stimson). Chosen over the same source's 'No regrets' page (the holder's Fox/WSJ lines, which the Fox cut carries in full) because this page is the test the 11-03 note set — 'the vote's clock runs out today; tomorrow's queue is the test' — and the only LI page in the queue on the Strait and the blockade; my call, one AJ per day

object.label: H6 — US control of the Strait of Hormuz (PG01, proposed 10-15): who holds the Strait the day after the vote, read from Tehran. The Strait's holder in his own words for the first time on the Press: 'the stage of the Persian Gulf, especially the Strait of Hormuz, has invalidated the myth of American invincibility'. The terms counted — seven conditions for partially reopening the Strait and a US first step (Azizi) — and the lock on the other side: a naval blockade and economic pressure on 90 million Iranians as Washington's instrument. The force runs through the page: Trump 'has talked about attacking Iran for weeks', the lame-duck period, limited strikes 'still possible'. The pump is not on the page except as 'the resulting economic crisis'

transformNote: the shadow is 'U.S. control' (the holder, 10-25 and earlier) and, at its strongest, the office's 'oil flows out of the Persian Gulf exceed pre-conflict levels' (aj 11-02, constitutive +0.7). On this page the Strait's other holder speaks for the first time and names it as the place American invincibility was invalidated; the analysts put the reopening behind seven conditions and the lifting of the blockade; the article has 'control in and around the Strait' still fought over. The vote enters as a verdict both capitals read — Tehran as a rejection of the war, the analysts as pressure for an off-ramp — and the force as the thing the vote may not stop

log.what: daily cut over the 11-04 sweep (GitHub copy). Twenty-six paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch; eighteen scored, three constitutive (Khamenei — the Strait's holder, first words on the Press), four sorted off the object (the anniversary marches, the reformist front page, the El-Sayed line). Object declared on H6 the day after the vote; the force (cand-post-election-strikes) carried as the page's second object and sorted, not declared — my call. Ghalibaf and Mohseni-Ejei stationed with the publication rather than @O (the Baghaei precedent: their lines are on the vote, not the Strait) — reversible

split.note: one station, two planes: the Iranian officials as reported run 40–55 (the vehicle is theirs — 'NO TO WAR', 'Nightmare', 'defeated in both war and politics'); the analysts run 14–26; the article's own lines 12–30 except the billboard (44). Rule 5: Vakil 16 → 24 → 18 → 14 (fluid throughout); Slavin 26 → 20 → 30. The split is between what Tehran says and what the readers measure, inside one page

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: Iranian leaders welcome the US midterms, but Trump may still attack; Tehran views the results as a rejection of the 'war on Iran'
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek): the vote as a verdict on the war, and the force in the same headline
lines.zWhy: a Strait whose other holder celebrates the vote is not a Strait under US control

lines.quote: in Tehran the authorities present the sweeping Republican defeats as the American public's rejection of the war
lines.note: the frame: the capital's reading of the vote
lines.zWhy: a capital reading the vote as its own win reads the Strait as held

lines.quote: Ghalibaf: 'Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR' — and Iran endorses the message; he led the delegation to the June MOU
lines.note: the speaker who signed the June MOU reads the vote; the pump is on the page here only, as 'the cost of living'
lines.zWhy: the party to the talks claiming the vote is the party setting the terms

lines.quote: if Washington betrays the public will to serve 'international paymasters and blackmailers', Iran's 'NO' comes with a 'Nightmare'
lines.note: denominated — the threat in capitals; the page's highest line
lines.zWhy: a threat attached to the vote is a Strait held as leverage

lines.quote: Mohseni-Ejei: 'Trump was defeated in both war and politics'; the Islamic republic will impose more defeats
lines.note: the judiciary's reading — denominated
lines.zWhy: 'defeated in war' is the Strait read from the winner's side

lines.quote: analysts: the Democratic sweep, which complicates the president's remaining years, will make Iran's leadership more adamant about its demands to end the war the US and Israel started on 28 February
lines.note: the mechanism: the vote hardens the terms; the war dated
lines.zWhy: a leadership more adamant is a Strait less open

lines.quote: Trump has talked about attacking Iran for weeks but says he has not decided; a US naval blockade, sanctions and trade disruption are also heavily pressuring Iran
lines.note: THE FORCE AND THE LOCK on one line — the strikes undecided, the blockade in force (the Fox 11-01 page dated it: 14 July)
lines.zWhy: a blockade as the pressure is a Strait contested, not controlled

lines.quote: Vakil: the Republican defeat increases pressure to end the war but does not rule out further strikes
lines.note: the reader's first line: pressure up, the force not off
lines.zWhy: pressure to end a war is not the war ended

lines.quote: Trump 'needs a diplomatic victory or at worst an off-ramp' but may be reluctant to look weak after defeat
lines.note: the off-ramp named; 'look weak' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: an off-ramp still needed reads neither way on the Strait

lines.quote: Azizi: Iran's sense of victory makes its leaders more uncompromising on core demands — seven conditions for partially reopening the Strait of Hormuz and a US first step
lines.note: THE TERMS, COUNTED: seven conditions — the fourth sighting of the terms (June MOU · 10-18 · 10-27 · 11-02) and the first with a number; 'partially' is new
lines.zWhy: seven conditions for a partial reopening is a Strait priced by its holder

lines.quote: Iran's chances of making nuclear concessions could be even lower than before
lines.note: right domain, wrong plane — the nuclear question, which Washington wants in any new talks (the AP wire, 11-02); surface-bound
lines.zWhy: fewer nuclear concessions is the deal further off, not the Strait itself

lines.quote: the stage of the Persian Gulf, especially the Strait of Hormuz, has invalidated the myth of American invincibility
lines.note: constitutive — THE STRAIT'S HOLDER, FIRST WORDS ON THE PRESS: a statement attributed to Khamenei for the embassy anniversary; he has not been seen or heard in public since March. The Strait named as the place the myth broke. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: some still hope that party changes or concessions in the US will end Iran's enmity — they are harshly mistaken
lines.note: constitutive — the vote disclaimed as a lever by the Strait's holder. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: the only route to absolute deterrence is pursuing strength
lines.note: constitutive — the doctrine unchanged (the AP wire 11-02: no change to the nuclear doctrine). Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: a giant billboard unveiled Tuesday in Enghelab Square: Trump behind bars, 'We will kill Trump'
lines.note: the article reports the billboard flat; the words are the billboard's — denominated as carried
lines.zWhy: a capital that bills the holder behind bars is not the Strait's junior party

lines.quote: Iran and the US continue to fight over control in and around the Strait of Hormuz; the Trump administration is counting on a blockade and economic pressure on 90 million Iranians to change Iran's behaviour
lines.note: H6 AS THE PAGE STATES IT: control contested; the blockade the instrument; the population sized
lines.zWhy: control still fought over is not control

lines.quote: Vakil expects intensified diplomacy alongside continued military threats over the coming weeks; limited strikes still possible
lines.note: the reader's forecast — both tracks at once
lines.zWhy: diplomacy with threats attached is a Strait still contested

lines.quote: 'an interim agreement over the Strait of Hormuz and the lifting of the blockade appears more realistic than a comprehensive settlement'
lines.note: THE READER'S FALSIFIER: the Strait and the blockade as one hinge — the shape the AP wire's conditions had (11-02); an interim deal is the test
lines.zWhy: an interim deal over the Strait is a Strait not yet open

lines.quote: Slavin: concerned Trump would use the 'lame duck' period to attack Iran again
lines.note: THE FORCE, from Washington's reader: the lame-duck window named as the force's window
lines.zWhy: an attack feared in the lame-duck window is the force not stood down

lines.quote: 'Trump still retains enormous powers as commander-in-chief'; the size of the Democratic victory makes all-out war less likely, in her view
lines.note: the force sized by the vote: smaller, not off
lines.zWhy: all-out war less likely is the force reduced, not removed

lines.quote: 'it is clear that the war and the resulting economic crisis defeated the Republicans'
lines.note: the gas↔votes predicate from Washington's think tank — 'economic crisis' is the pump's only trace on the page
lines.zWhy: a war that defeated a party by its economic crisis is the price's verdict, unnumbered
